3:103.ar: وَٱعۡتَصِمُواْ بِحَبۡلِ ٱللَّهِ جَمِيعࣰ ا وَلَا تَفَرَّقُواْۚ وَٱذۡكُرُواْ نِعۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡ إِذۡ كُنتُمۡ أَعۡدَآءࣰ فَأَلَّفَ بَيۡنَ قُلُوبِكُمۡ فَأَصۡبَحۡتُم بِنِعۡمَتِهِۦٓ إِخۡوَٰنࣰ ا وَكُنتُمۡ عَلَىٰ شَفَا حُفۡرَةࣲ مِّنَ ٱلنَّارِ فَأَنقَذَكُم مِّنۡهَاۗ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَهۡتَدُونَ
3:103.en: And hold fast, all of you together, to the cable of Allah, and do not separate. And remember Allah's favour unto you: How ye were enemies and He made friendship between your hearts so that ye became as brothers by His grace; and (how) ye were upon the brink of an abyss of fire, and He did save you from it. Thus Allah maketh clear His revelations unto you, that haply ye may be guided

3:105.ar: وَلَا تَكُونُواْ كَٱلَّذِينَ تَفَرَّقُواْ وَٱخۡتَلَفُواْ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَهُمُ ٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتُۚ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمۡ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
3:105.en: And be ye not as those who separated and disputed after the clear proofs had come unto them. For such there is an awful doom

20:94.ar: قَالَ يَبۡنَؤُمَّ لَا تَأۡخُذۡ بِلِحۡيَتِي وَلَا بِرَأۡسِيٓۖ إِنِّي خَشِيتُ أَن تَقُولَ فَرَّقۡتَ بَيۡنَ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ وَلَمۡ تَرۡقُبۡ قَوۡلِي
20:94.en: He said: O son of my mother! Clutch not my beard nor my head! I feared lest thou shouldst say: Thou hast caused division among the Children of Israel, and hast not waited for my word

6:159.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ فَرَّقُواْ دِينَهُمۡ وَكَانُواْ شِيَعࣰ ا لَّسۡتَ مِنۡهُمۡ فِي شَيۡءٍۚ إِنَّمَآ أَمۡرُهُمۡ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُنَبِّئُهُم بِمَا كَانُواْ يَفۡعَلُونَ
6:159.en: Lo! As for those who sunder their religion and become schismatics, no concern at all hast thou with them. Their case will go to Allah, Who then will tell them what they used to do

11:87.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰشُعَيۡبُ أَصَلَوٰتُكَ تَأۡمُرُكَ أَن نَّتۡرُكَ مَا يَعۡبُدُ ءَابَآؤُنَآ أَوۡ أَن نَّفۡعَلَ فِيٓ أَمۡوَٰلِنَا مَا نَشَٰٓؤُاْۖ إِنَّكَ لَأَنتَ ٱلۡحَلِيمُ ٱلرَّشِيدُ
11:87.en: They said: O Shu'eyb! Doth thy way of prayer command thee that we should forsake that which our fathers (used to) worship, or that we (should leave off) doing what we will with our own property. Lo! thou art the mild, the guide to right behaviour

11:62.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰصَٰلِحُ قَدۡ كُنتَ فِينَا مَرۡجُوࣰّ ا قَبۡلَ هَٰذَآۖ أَتَنۡهَىٰنَآ أَن نَّعۡبُدَ مَا يَعۡبُدُ ءَابَآؤُنَا وَإِنَّنَا لَفِي شَكࣲّ مِّمَّا تَدۡعُونَآ إِلَيۡهِ مُرِيبࣲ‏
11:62.en: They said: O Salih! Thou hast been among us hitherto as that wherein our hope was placed. Dost thou ask us not to worship what our fathers worshipped? Lo! we verily are in grave doubt concerning that to which thou callest us

TP481OJ2XFU.speaker: adnan
TP481OJ2XFU.speaker_note: mentions ten years speaking to university students, being in his late 30s, and London, Ontario community politics
TP481OJ2XFU.title: My Maxims, Part 4
TP481OJ2XFU.one_line: Students hold the power to shift narratives; then two maxims: division is evil, and Islam without reform is toothless.
TP481OJ2XFU.summary: He opens with the student encampments spreading across campuses, including the one at Western now in its third day. People in their twenties hold the power to set what society finds reasonable, which is why the Prophet invested in the young, and he holds up Ali running some 400 km to Medina barefoot after sleeping in the Prophet's bed. The community must educate, mentor and support its students, whose demand that institutions practise the ethics they teach is humanitarian, not partisan. He then explains that the series sets out his own maxims so imams and congregants can find common ground. The first maxim is that dividing the ummah is evil. From the verses on holding to Allah's rope, Harun's fear of splitting Bani Israel, and the verse on those who split their religion, he argues that division also includes refusing to collaborate and resisting change out of closed-mindedness, and that each decision should be weighed for its effect on unity. He chides those who discuss world politics while ignoring a messy local backyard. The second maxim is that Islam without reform is lifeless: people come to the masjid to change, accepting people is not accepting the status quo, and every prophet, like Shuayb, confronted the one problem that could sink his society.

outline.heading: Opening
Students hold the power to shift narratives
outline.gist: Students across campuses are speaking out through peaceful encampments. Every institution needs the blessing of people in their twenties; most are easily manipulated, but when that age group decides something must change, it changes regardless of money or politics.

outline.heading: Why the Prophet invested in the young
outline.gist: Life beats passion out of older adults with kids, mortgages and jobs. That is why the Prophet gave his attention to Ali and to teenagers others would not bother speaking to: people that age can force the hand of the oppressor.

outline.heading: Ali's run to Medina
outline.gist: After sleeping in the Prophet's bed and returning the trusts, Ali ran some 400 km to Medina with no mount and arrived barefoot, out of love. Putting a lid on the young gets nowhere: educate, mentor and empower them.

outline.heading: Back the students at the Western encampment
outline.gist: On its third day the students are staying until their demands are met. Their demand is humanitarian, not partisan: that the institution teaching them ethics practise them. The community must support them.

outline.heading: Why he lays out his maxims
outline.gist: The imams say one thing, people hear another and expect a third, so everyone lives in separate silos. Explaining where he comes from may create the common ground needed to fix problems complained about for decades.

outline.heading: Maxim 1: dividing the ummah is evil
outline.gist: Dividing the ummah is pure evil with no good excuse, and the Quran says so repeatedly.

outline.heading: Hold to Allah's rope and do not split
outline.gist: Imams quote the verse on holding to Allah's rope and stop, but it goes on to forbid being like those who split and fought after clear proofs came.

outline.heading: Harun would not divide Bani Israel
outline.gist: Facing the golden calf, Harun held back and waited for Musa because speaking out would have split the people, showing how seriously the Quran treats division.

outline.heading: Those who split their religion
outline.gist: The Prophet is told he has nothing to do with those who split their religion. Fear of division is still no excuse to do nothing or to brand every other stance as divisive.

outline.heading: Intolerance and refusing to collaborate are division
outline.gist: When people ask a masjid for changes that suit them, the one defending the status quo is the divider if he lacks tolerance and cannot see others' needs.

outline.heading: Closed-mindedness is a source of division
outline.gist: Refusing to change an unhealthy way of doing things because it has always been so makes you the cause of division. Ask of every decision whether it will divide the ummah.

outline.heading: Bend over backwards for unity, starting locally
outline.gist: Sacrifice and work with people you dislike to keep the community together. The global ummah is beyond our reach, so start with a small community like this one.

outline.heading: World politics with a messy backyard
outline.gist: His pet peeve: people discuss rulers they cannot influence while ignoring local problems they could fix with a little effort for the next generation.

outline.heading: Care for everyone equally; the path of falsehood
outline.gist: Every group must be cared for equally whatever its origin or language. Falsehood looks attractive for a while but ends in darkness; truth may start dark but ends in light.

outline.heading: Interlude
Maxim 2: Islam without reform is toothless
outline.gist: Without islah, from the heart up to how the world is governed, Islam becomes an opioid or a carcass, and attendance dwindles from daily to yearly.

outline.heading: People come to the masjid to change
outline.gist: People come looking in the book for solutions and to become better, and want that to spread to the community and the world. That requires an Islam able to say a mistake must change.

outline.heading: Accepting people is not accepting the status quo
outline.gist: Everyone is welcome whoever they are, but not so that everything they do is celebrated; they come to start becoming better.

outline.heading: Reform together, without judging
outline.gist: We fix our shortcomings as a jamaah, and since everyone has faults there is no point judging. Without reform a religion is a social gathering that strokes egos.

outline.heading: Every prophet was a reformist: Shuayb
outline.gist: Prophets addressed what their society needed to change. Shuayb kept naming his people's cheating in trade instead of praising their pleasant manners.

outline.heading: One unchallenged problem sinks a society
outline.gist: A single problem left unchallenged is enough to sink a society. Every people asked their prophet to let one thing go, as Madyan asked whether they really had to change what they did with their wealth.

outline.heading: Come as you are, then accept Islam as it is
outline.gist: The moment a prophet challenged a wrong, his people said they used to like him. Islam without reform adds nothing; find what is missing in yourself and the community and work on it.

outline.heading: Outro

5:25.ar: قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي لَآ أَمۡلِكُ إِلَّا نَفۡسِي وَأَخِيۖ فَٱفۡرُقۡ بَيۡنَنَا وَبَيۡنَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
5:25.en: He said: My Lord! I have control of none but myself and my brother, so distinguish between us and the wrong-doing folk

5:26.ar: قَالَ فَإِنَّهَا مُحَرَّمَةٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡۛ أَرۡبَعِينَ سَنَةࣰۛ يَتِيهُونَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ فَلَا تَأۡسَ عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡفَٰسِقِينَ
5:26.en: (Their Lord) said: For this the land will surely be forbidden them for forty years that they will wander in the earth, bewildered. So grieve not over the wrongdoing folk

11:87.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰشُعَيۡبُ أَصَلَوٰتُكَ تَأۡمُرُكَ أَن نَّتۡرُكَ مَا يَعۡبُدُ ءَابَآؤُنَآ أَوۡ أَن نَّفۡعَلَ فِيٓ أَمۡوَٰلِنَا مَا نَشَٰٓؤُاْۖ إِنَّكَ لَأَنتَ ٱلۡحَلِيمُ ٱلرَّشِيدُ
11:87.en: They said: O Shu'eyb! Doth thy way of prayer command thee that we should forsake that which our fathers (used to) worship, or that we (should leave off) doing what we will with our own property. Lo! thou art the mild, the guide to right behaviour

11:113.ar: وَلَا تَرۡكَنُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ فَتَمَسَّكُمُ ٱلنَّارُ وَمَا لَكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مِنۡ أَوۡلِيَآءَ ثُمَّ لَا تُنصَرُونَ
11:113.en: And incline not toward those who do wrong lest the Fire touch you, and ye have no protecting friends against Allah, and afterward ye would not be helped

11:62.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰصَٰلِحُ قَدۡ كُنتَ فِينَا مَرۡجُوࣰّ ا قَبۡلَ هَٰذَآۖ أَتَنۡهَىٰنَآ أَن نَّعۡبُدَ مَا يَعۡبُدُ ءَابَآؤُنَا وَإِنَّنَا لَفِي شَكࣲّ مِّمَّا تَدۡعُونَآ إِلَيۡهِ مُرِيبࣲ‏
11:62.en: They said: O Salih! Thou hast been among us hitherto as that wherein our hope was placed. Dost thou ask us not to worship what our fathers worshipped? Lo! we verily are in grave doubt concerning that to which thou callest us

11:27.ar: فَقَالَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن قَوۡمِهِۦ مَا نَرَىٰكَ إِلَّا بَشَرࣰ ا مِّثۡلَنَا وَمَا نَرَىٰكَ ٱتَّبَعَكَ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ هُمۡ أَرَاذِلُنَا بَادِيَ ٱلرَّأۡيِ وَمَا نَرَىٰ لَكُمۡ عَلَيۡنَا مِن فَضۡلِۭ بَلۡ نَظُنُّكُمۡ كَٰذِبِينَ
11:27.en: The chieftains of his folk, who disbelieved, said: We see thee but a mortal like us, and we see not that any follow thee save the most abject among us, without reflection. We behold in you no merit above us - nay, we deem you liars

11:28.ar: قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِن كُنتُ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّي وَءَاتَىٰنِي رَحۡمَةࣰ مِّنۡ عِندِهِۦ فَعُمِّيَتۡ عَلَيۡكُمۡ أَنُلۡزِمُكُمُوهَا وَأَنتُمۡ لَهَا كَٰرِهُونَ
11:28.en: He said: O my people! Bethink you, if I rely on a clear proof from my Lord and there hath come unto me a mercy from His presence, and it hath been made obscure to you, can we compel you to accept it when ye are averse thereto

11:29.ar: وَيَٰقَوۡمِ لَآ أَسۡـَٔلُكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِ مَالًاۖ إِنۡ أَجۡرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱللَّهِۚ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ بِطَارِدِ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْۚ إِنَّهُم مُّلَٰقُواْ رَبِّهِمۡ وَلَٰكِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰكُمۡ قَوۡمࣰ ا تَجۡهَلُونَ
11:29.en: And O my people! I ask of you no wealth therefor. My reward is the concern only of Allah, and I am not going to thrust away those who believe - Lo! they have to meet their Lord! - but I see you a folk that are ignorant

PIAzoYYdAWM.speaker: adnan
PIAzoYYdAWM.speaker_note: refers to last week's maxim, his life in Syria and students at Western; his usual series voice
PIAzoYYdAWM.title: My Maxims, Part 5
PIAzoYYdAWM.one_line: On the 76th Nakba anniversary, he argues Islam is reform, every prophet targeted his people's one deficit, and ours is passivity toward injustice.
PIAzoYYdAWM.summary: Marking 76 years since the Nakba, he criticizes the predictable Muslim response to Palestine: outrage and protests while bombs fall, then back to business as usual, which the other side has learned to simply outlast. Nothing lasts forever and the Holy Land was occupied longer before, so the question is not hope but what kind of generation will fix it. History shows only people who make justice their first priority, not a part-time interest, change their destiny, and they should expect no thanks except from Allah. Otherwise, like the Israelites who refused to follow Musa, the task waits for a later generation. Repeating last week's maxim that Islam without reform is not Islam, he shows from the stories of Shuayb, Lut, Hud, Salih and Nuh that each prophet confronted the one deficit of his people and refused to change the subject, and that people were judged by that deficit, not their other merits. The same holds personally: your story is what you are not doing right. In the second khutbah he explains the Quranic warning against growing comfortable with oppressors, criticizes rulers who love an Islam stripped of reform, and asks people to tie their personal and communal work to clear goals and to visit the Western encampment.

outline.heading: Opening
76 years since the Nakba
outline.gist: The Palestinians were driven from their land 76 years ago, and today the attempt to erase them from the land of their forefathers looks much like yesterday.

outline.heading: Our predictable outrage
outline.gist: Each bombing brings red faces, loud voices and a few weeks of protest, then business as usual with the companies and friends who back it. The other side has learned to simply outlast us.

outline.heading: No empowered group, no plan
outline.gist: It has stayed in the news only because the bombing has not stopped for eight months. No group has been given the community's full support to keep pushing, and no plan exists for when it ends.

outline.heading: The Holy Land was freed before
outline.gist: It was occupied for longer earlier in Islamic history and still freed, so there is no reason to lose hope. The question is what kind of generation will fix it.

outline.heading: A generation that puts righteousness first
outline.gist: Only people who treat justice and opposing oppression as priorities nothing trumps will change things. History shows no people ever freed themselves treating it as a part-time interest.

outline.heading: Give everything and expect no thanks
outline.gist: Those who changed their destiny gave everything without waiting for reward. No one will stand by you or thank you except Allah, and if we cannot accept that, we wait.

outline.heading: Musa and the forty years of wandering
outline.gist: Musa was ready but had only himself and Harun, so the land was forbidden to his people for forty years and the next generation entered it.

outline.heading: Then I will talk about something popular
outline.gist: Sarcastically he offers to preach on whatever people request instead. If righteousness does not trump everything and we will not speak against oppression, all this is a waste of time.

outline.heading: Live for it; you do not have to die for it
outline.gist: Others paid with their blood; we only have to direct our academic, social and financial lives toward strengthening the cause, which can be harder.

outline.heading: Restating the maxim: without reform Islam is not Islam
outline.gist: Reform means seeing where a people's problem is. Coming to a people with a deficit and talking about something else is a betrayal.

outline.heading: Shuayb's people ask two questions
outline.gist: They ask whether his prayer commands them to change whom they worship and what they do with their wealth. Every prophet began with tawhid, then the specific deficit.

outline.heading: Shuayb would not change the subject
outline.gist: He could have preached humility and kindness and become popular, but he kept naming their cheating with money until it was fixed.

outline.heading: Lut and Hud named their people's one problem
outline.gist: Lut addressed only the behaviour that had to stop; Hud confronted the racism and arrogance of Ad, not finances, because that was their problem.

outline.heading: This generation will be asked about injustice
outline.gist: We will be questioned about the injustices we witnessed and did little about, and listing other good deeds will not answer that question.

outline.heading: Judged by the deficit, not the merits
outline.gist: Shuayb's people were judged by their finances, not their manners, and destroyed when they did not fix it. A community's other merits are Allah's gifts anyway.

outline.heading: Your story is what you are not doing right
outline.gist: Personally, your story is what you know you are not doing right. No presentation of your strengths will help, since the rest was given to you; that weak spot is what you will be asked about.

outline.heading: Not wealth or numbers but willpower
outline.gist: We focus on other things and feel ashamed only while the bombing lasts. In 76 years Muslim communities have built no advocacy with teeth; the lack is willpower, commitment and understanding of what we will be judged on.

outline.heading: Interlude
Do not grow comfortable with oppressors
outline.gist: The verse near the end of Surah Hud forbids growing chummy with wrongdoers, or the Fire will touch you and no one will stand by you. Stand clearly against what you know is oppressive.

outline.heading: Salih and Hud fought one issue each
outline.gist: Study the Quran through the prophets' stories: each fought his people on one issue. Salih's people said they had hopes for him until he called out their wastefulness; Hud told Ad to stop oppressing others and being racist.

outline.heading: Nuh would not dismiss his poor followers
outline.gist: After 950 years his people offered to believe if he removed the lowly or held separate sessions for rich and poor. He compromised on everything but that.

outline.heading: Our deficit: letting injustice slide
outline.gist: Equality was the deficit Nuh came to fix. Ours is that injustices keep happening while we take no clear stand against them and let too much slide.

outline.heading: Dictators love Islam without reform
outline.gist: We are normalizing what the Quran forbids. Rulers are happy with bigger masjids, better sound systems and full rows as long as no one speaks against dictatorship or corruption.

outline.heading: Syria: anything but oppression
outline.gist: Living in Syria he could speak about anything except the glaring oppression, and that version of religion failed. Speaking out must cost us, or we wander for forty years.

outline.heading: Why not this generation
outline.gist: One generation will do it, so start the push now even if we never see the result. Education, mentorship and outreach continue, but tied to clearly defined goals.

outline.heading: Back the students at Western
outline.gist: Drop in to show solidarity with the encampment. Help that age group believe it can make a difference, and give it experienced counsel.

outline.heading: Outro

63:7.ar: هُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ لَا تُنفِقُواْ عَلَىٰ مَنۡ عِندَ رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ حَتَّىٰ يَنفَضُّواْۗ وَلِلَّهِ خَزَآئِنُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقِينَ لَا يَفۡقَهُونَ
63:7.en: They it is who say: Spend not on behalf of those (who dwell) with Allah's messenger that they may disperse (and go away from you); when Allah's are the treasures of the heavens and the earth; but the hypocrites comprehend not

63:8.ar: يَقُولُونَ لَئِن رَّجَعۡنَآ إِلَى ٱلۡمَدِينَةِ لَيُخۡرِجَنَّ ٱلۡأَعَزُّ مِنۡهَا ٱلۡأَذَلَّۚ وَلِلَّهِ ٱلۡعِزَّةُ وَلِرَسُولِهِۦ وَلِلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقِينَ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
63:8.en: They say: Surely, if we return to Al-Madinah the mightier will soon drive out the weaker; when might belongeth to Allah and to His messenger and to the believers; but the hypocrites know not

63:9.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تُلۡهِكُمۡ أَمۡوَٰلُكُمۡ وَلَآ أَوۡلَٰدُكُمۡ عَن ذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِۚ وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡ ذَٰلِكَ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡخَٰسِرُونَ
63:9.en: O ye who believe! Let not your wealth nor your children distract you from remembrance of Allah. Those who do so, they are the losers

63:10.ar: وَأَنفِقُواْ مِن مَّا رَزَقۡنَٰكُم مِّن قَبۡلِ أَن يَأۡتِيَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ فَيَقُولَ رَبِّ لَوۡلَآ أَخَّرۡتَنِيٓ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلࣲ قَرِيبࣲ فَأَصَّدَّقَ وَأَكُن مِّنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
63:10.en: And spend of that wherewith We have provided you before death cometh unto one of you and he saith: My Lord! If only thou wouldst reprieve me for a little while, then I would give alms and be among the righteous

63:11.ar: وَلَن يُؤَخِّرَ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهَاۚ وَٱللَّهُ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ
63:11.en: But Allah reprieveth no soul when its term cometh, and Allah is Informed of what ye do

9:84.ar: وَلَا تُصَلِّ عَلَىٰٓ أَحَدࣲ مِّنۡهُم مَّاتَ أَبَدࣰ ا وَلَا تَقُمۡ عَلَىٰ قَبۡرِهِۦٓۖ إِنَّهُمۡ كَفَرُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَمَاتُواْ وَهُمۡ فَٰسِقُونَ

LhX1xqL3vdw.speaker: adnan
LhX1xqL3vdw.speaker_note: Sunday tafseer series at MWN; concludes his own series on the surah
LhX1xqL3vdw.title: Surat Al-Munafiqun, Part 3 (Verses 8-11)
LhX1xqL3vdw.one_line: Al-Munafiqun 8-11: carrying your weight, Ibn Ubayy's racist threat and the Prophet's restraint, true honour, and two safeguards against hypocrisy.
LhX1xqL3vdw.summary: He recaps the surah's core claim that the community's real enemy is within: freeloaders who take every benefit and give nothing. Believers must beware of them without labelling, excluding or fighting anyone, and use the descriptions to examine themselves. Expeditions required each fighter to bring his own provisions, which he turns into a challenge for his own community: contribute time, skills or money to the masjid rather than treating it as a free service, and act in ways that would work if everyone did the same. Verse 8 tells the story of the quarrel at a well on the expedition, the Prophet's rebuke of tribal rallying calls as rotten, and Ibn Ubayy's boast that the mighty would expel the lowly from Madinah, which he calls collective arrogance, the essence of racism. The Prophet refused to have him killed, honoured his son, and later prayed over him, while the son barred his father from entering Madinah without the Prophet's permission. Honour belongs to Allah, His Messenger and the believers. The closing verses give two safeguards: do not let wealth and family distract you from the purpose you were created for, and give from whatever you have before death arrives and you beg for a little more time. He recommends imagining your own death to regain perspective.

outline.heading: Opening
Recap: the comprehensive surahs and the organizational cluster
outline.gist: Juz 28's surahs organize relationships among Muslims, with non-Muslims, the social contract, leadership and finally the hypocrites.

outline.heading: The true enemy comes from within
outline.gist: For the community as for the individual, the real problem is inside, not across the fence.

outline.heading: Beware, but never exclude or fight
outline.gist: Do not let freeloaders ruin your progress, but you may not remove them; Surat At-Tawbah gives the detail.

outline.heading: The carriage: pushers, riders and those pushing back
outline.gist: Most of the work is done by a tiny fraction while many simply ride along and take the perks.

outline.heading: Never label anyone a hypocrite
outline.gist: Even the Prophet did not expose those he knew; the descriptions are warnings for oneself, and hypocrisy is a spectrum.

outline.heading: No freeloading on expeditions
outline.gist: Fighters had to bring their own mount, food and shoes or stay behind excused, while the wealthy equipped others.

outline.heading: Carry your weight in the masjid
outline.gist: People use classes, funerals and the cemetery and show up for Eid prayers without contributing; he prefers not to charge but expects everyone to give time, skills or money.

outline.heading: Recap: withholding provisions to break the companions
outline.gist: The hypocrites refused to share when the expedition ran three times longer than planned.

outline.heading: Act as if everyone would copy you
outline.gist: Like pandemic hoarding, behaviour that would collapse the system if everyone did it makes you part of the problem.

outline.heading: Four kinds of people
outline.gist: The one who knows and knows it, knows but forgot it, is ignorant and knows it, and is ignorant without knowing; avoid the last.

outline.heading: Interlude
"The mightier will expel the lowlier"
outline.gist: Double emphasis in their threat, with Ibn Ubayy meaning himself and the Prophet and his followers.

outline.heading: The quarrel at the well: "Leave it, it is rotten"
outline.gist: A shove between a Muhajir and an Ansari became tribal rallying cries; the Prophet ran out half-dressed and condemned the calls of jahiliyyah that once fuelled decades of feuds.

outline.heading: Ibn Ubayy's insult, and racism as collective arrogance
outline.gist: He compared the Muslims to a dog that eats its feeder; believing one's group superior is arrogance multiplied.

outline.heading: The boy who reported it
outline.gist: Zayd ibn Arqam told the Prophet, who questioned him repeatedly to teach him not to spread such talk.

outline.heading: "Muhammad does not kill his companions"
outline.gist: Umar suggested execution; the Prophet refused and insisted on treating him well as long as he outwardly remained with them.

outline.heading: The son's offer
outline.gist: Abdullah, Ibn Ubayy's believing son, asked to carry out any execution himself rather than live seeing his father's killer; the Prophet again refused.

outline.heading: Forgiving the man whose crown he took
outline.gist: Despite twelve documented harms, the Prophet kept forgiving, then prayed over him and shrouded him in his own garment for his son's sake before revelation forbade it; death should end grudges.

outline.heading: Honour belongs to Allah, His Messenger and the believers
outline.gist: True honour is what lasts into eternity; hypocrites do not know where wealth and honour come from, so they hoard and ally with the strong.

outline.heading: Ask the elderly what mattered
outline.gist: People in their eighties and nineties say to live by what you believe is right, since life passes in a moment.

outline.heading: The son at the gate of Madinah
outline.gist: Abdullah barred his father from entering until the Prophet permitted it, and the Prophet told him to let his father in and treat him kindly.

outline.heading: Summary: the hypocrite's traits in the surah
outline.gist: Claims without commitment, polished surface, guilt, disrespect for the Prophet, withholding wealth and reviving tribal and national divisions; reflect on them in yourself.

outline.heading: Interlude
Lahw: being distracted from the priority
outline.gist: Distraction can be pointless fun or a worthwhile task at the wrong time, like tidying your room before an exam.

outline.heading: Wealth and children: financial and social support
outline.gist: Amwal and awlad stand for financial and social needs; no one in a Muslim community should be lonely, as distinct from alone.

outline.heading: Don't let the gifts distract from the purpose
outline.gist: Allah made the world for you and you for Him; enjoy wealth and family and use them to draw closer, not live for them.

outline.heading: The real losers, and families entering Paradise together
outline.gist: Those distracted by blessings lose them all; those who used them well find wealth and children waiting for them.

outline.heading: Give from what We provided
outline.gist: Rizq includes time, knowledge and skills; infaq, sharing a root with nifaq, is giving that disappears with nothing expected back.

outline.heading: Rehearse your own death
outline.gist: An early scholar would lie in a narrow space imagining his death, then rise saying he had another chance; the exercise brings perspective and joy.

outline.heading: "If only You delayed me": sadaqah proves the claim
outline.gist: The dying ask for a little time to give in charity; sadaqah is proof of truthfulness, answering the hypocrites' empty testimony.

outline.heading: No delay, and every breath is a second chance
outline.gist: When the term comes there is no extension; any time not guaranteed to you is a second chance.

outline.heading: Khabir: He knows the hidden truth
outline.gist: The closing name points to inner states only Allah knows; the two safeguards are not being distracted and giving now.

64:1.ar: يُسَبِّحُ لِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ لَهُ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ وَلَهُ ٱلۡحَمۡدُۖ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرٌ
64:1.en: All that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth glorifieth Allah; unto Him belongeth Sovereignty and unto Him belongeth praise, and He is Able to do all things

64:2.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُمۡ فَمِنكُمۡ كَافِرࣱ وَمِنكُم مُّؤۡمِنࣱۚ وَٱللَّهُ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ
64:2.en: He it is Who created you, but one of you is a disbeliever and one of you is a believer, and Allah is Seer of what ye do

64:3.ar: خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَصَوَّرَكُمۡ فَأَحۡسَنَ صُوَرَكُمۡۖ وَإِلَيۡهِ ٱلۡمَصِيرُ
64:3.en: He created the heavens and the earth with truth, and He shaped you and made good your shapes, and unto Him is the journeying

64:4.ar: يَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا تُسِرُّونَ وَمَا تُعۡلِنُونَۚ وَٱللَّهُ عَلِيمُۢ بِذَاتِ ٱلصُّدُورِ
64:4.en: He knoweth all that is in the heavens and the earth, and He knoweth what ye conceal and what ye publish. And Allah is Aware of what is in the breasts (of men)

2:170.ar: وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱتَّبِعُواْ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ قَالُواْ بَلۡ نَتَّبِعُ مَآ أَلۡفَيۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ ءَابَآءَنَآۚ أَوَلَوۡ كَانَ ءَابَآؤُهُمۡ لَا يَعۡقِلُونَ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا يَهۡتَدُونَ
2:170.en: And when it is said unto them: Follow that which Allah hath revealed, they say: We follow that wherein we found our fathers. What! Even though their fathers were wholly unintelligent and had no guidance

59:24.ar: هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡخَٰلِقُ ٱلۡبَارِئُ ٱلۡمُصَوِّرُۖ لَهُ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءُ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰۚ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
59:24.en: He is Allah, the Creator, the Shaper out of naught, the Fashioner. His are the most beautiful names. All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifieth Him, and He is the Mighty, the Wise

Lx83VHAm9wE.speaker: adnan
Lx83VHAm9wE.speaker_note: His own Sunday tafseer series, opening a new surah
Lx83VHAm9wE.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Taghabun, Part 1 (64:1-4)
Lx83VHAm9wE.one_line: Al-Taghabun as the reminder of why we act: exalting Allah, purposeful creation, and the intentions He knows behind every deed.
Lx83VHAm9wE.summary: He presents Al-Taghabun as a Madani surah with a Makki flavour, placed among technical, ruling-heavy surahs to remind believers why they do any of it. When practice loses its purpose of pleasing Allah it hardens into custom, like an engagement procession that has forgotten its role as a guarantee of accountability, and means such as a masjid or institution become ends in themselves, which is corruption. Taghabun, from deception in trade, names the day when it becomes clear who fooled whom. He explains tasbih as exalting Allah beyond any flaw, a level above praise that means never questioning Him, grounded in His kingship, praiseworthiness and power, and illustrates the harm of zeal without purpose with a Syrian story of two responses to a man who prayed only Fajr. Kufr is denying a blessing, above all creation, and belief is proven by how one lives. Creation bil-haqq means purposefully; through Al-Khaliq, Al-Bari and Al-Musawwir he argues that sawwara means giving purpose, not shaping appearance. People who know their purpose live differently, as the Prophet did, and emulating him counts most where it is hardest. Allah knows what is in the chests, so intention is decisive: act for Allah, not one's group, and ask whether you could bear never being thanked.

outline.heading: A Madani surah with a Makki flavour
outline.gist: Among the organizational Madani surahs, Al-Taghabun reads like a Makki surah in its wording and tone.

outline.heading: Purpose as the safety valve
outline.gist: Spiritual passages amid technical rulings keep the purpose of pleasing Allah in view, so practice never turns harmful or tribal.

outline.heading: Its place after the organizational surahs
outline.gist: After surahs on relationships, citizenship, the social contract, leadership and hypocrisy, this surah adds that without purpose everything collapses.

outline.heading: When practices become customs: following the fathers
outline.gist: Practices no longer measured against pleasing Allah mutate into culture, like Quraysh following their fathers without asking whether they were guided.

outline.heading: Empty rituals and the next generation
outline.gist: Rituals reduced to skeletons stop making people better, and the next generation walks away from them.

outline.heading: The engagement procession that forgot its purpose
outline.gist: The large group accompanying a proposal was meant to show both bride and groom have people they answer to; it became showing off, traffic jams and waste.

outline.heading: The meaning of taghabun
outline.gist: Ghabn is deception in trade through ignorance or concealment; the Day of Judgment is when it becomes clear who fooled whom.

outline.heading: When the means become the goal
outline.gist: Once an institution's survival matters more than its function, it is corrupt, as with a company that cuts quality just to survive.

outline.heading: The masjid is a means, not an end
outline.gist: The goal is education, mentorship, unity, outreach and advocacy; do not build or expand for its own sake.

outline.heading: The day all deceit fades
outline.gist: Those who thought they were fooling others will find themselves the ones fooled before Allah.

outline.heading: Interlude
The last opening of tasbih in the juz
outline.gist: The repeated openings of exaltation through these surahs are gathered and explained here.

outline.heading: Technicality without purpose breeds harshness
outline.gist: Those who think the purpose is doing it right yell at people in the masjid for mistakes, driving them away instead of pleasing Allah.

outline.heading: The man who prayed only Fajr
outline.gist: A Syrian story: one man scolded him until he quit; another praised him and added Dhuhr, remembering the goal.

outline.heading: Tasbih: exaltation beyond praise
outline.gist: Praise, respect and obedience can be given to people; exalting means declaring someone beyond any flaw we could identify, which is for Allah alone.

outline.heading: Exalting means never questioning Him
outline.gist: We do not hold Allah to account or ask for a break; everything else in creation exalts Him and humans alone choose.

outline.heading: To Him belongs all sovereignty and praise
outline.gist: Allah literally owns us, body and soul, unlike any human ownership, and is always worthy of praise.

outline.heading: Exaltation ties every command to its purpose
outline.gist: Because He is King, Praiseworthy and Omnipotent, His commands cannot be weighed like a ruler's and must be connected to the objectives He set.

outline.heading: Interlude
Kufr as denying a blessing
outline.gist: Kufr means covering or refusing to acknowledge a favour; denying the blessing of creation became synonymous with disbelief.

outline.heading: Al-Basir: belief proven by how you live
outline.gist: Whether one acknowledges the Creator shows in behaviour, which Allah sees.

outline.heading: Created bil-haqq: purposefully
outline.gist: Haqq here is the opposite of aimlessness: creation has a goal, a plot and an ending.

outline.heading: The other reading: creation runs on justice
outline.gist: Reading haqq as justice is valid elsewhere, but here the context points to purpose.

outline.heading: Al-Khaliq: from nothing to something
outline.gist: Creating from absolute nothingness, without time or space, is beyond human comprehension.

outline.heading: Al-Bari: from no life to life
outline.gist: Science studies how the universe and the first cell work, not where the first matter or life came from.

outline.heading: Al-Musawwir: the granter of purpose
outline.gist: Surah means a design with an objective; science cannot answer why every living thing wants to live, grow and survive.

outline.heading: Shaped for a purpose, not for looks
outline.gist: Our selfish earthly side and our selfless higher side, like a tree's form, exist to serve a purpose; translating sawwara as appearance is a poor reading.

outline.heading: Not about beauty: purpose for every person
outline.gist: Some are born with deformities, so the verse cannot mean beauty; our bodies and minds are made the way they are so we can achieve something.

outline.heading: People who know why they are here live differently
outline.gist: Returning to Allah forces the question of purpose; those who answer it value different things and work selflessly for decades.

outline.heading: The Prophet as a new paradigm of a human being
outline.gist: His opponents could find no selfish motive in him, so people either fled from him or attached themselves to him for life.

outline.heading: He made it look effortless
outline.gist: Like a grandmaster or a tennis player, he made his way of living look easy; try it and you find it is not.

outline.heading: Emulate him where it hurts
outline.gist: Following the Sunnah counts in the one difficult relationship, desire or fear you avoid, not only where it is easy.

outline.heading: Returning to Him: the widening circle of caregiving
outline.gist: As khalifah and servant, one's responsibility grows from self to siblings, spouse, children, parents and community.

outline.heading: Interlude
He knows what is in the chests
outline.gist: Allah knows what we hide and reveal, down to fleeting thoughts, fears and envy that never become actions.

outline.heading: The four verses as a portrait of Allah
outline.gist: Exalted, King, Praiseworthy, Omnipotent, Creator, Seer, purposeful Designer and All-Knowing, ending with knowledge of the heart.

outline.heading: Right deed, wrong reason, goes nowhere
outline.gist: A visible good deed must be built on selflessness, humility and love; arrogance or envy inside empties it.

outline.heading: A concise description of Allah amid a technical juz
outline.gist: No other part of the juz describes Allah so densely, so that we remember why we do all the rest.

outline.heading: Ask why you do what you do
outline.gist: If everyone asked who they are serving, behaviour and outcomes would change; what matters most is why something was done.

outline.heading: For Allah, not for my group
outline.gist: Once work is for one's race, nation or group it becomes the law of the jungle; for Allah it carries a higher moral standard.

outline.heading: The test: could you bear never being thanked?
outline.gist: If you need loyalty, votes or praise in return, say so honestly; doing it for Allah means wanting it never mentioned again.

outline.heading: Don't fool yourself
outline.gist: Doing things for Allah, by His teachings, protects communities from harm and arrogance, which is why the surah sits before the most technical one.

themes.label: Intention and sincerity (niyyah, ikhlas)
themes.note: Practice detached from the purpose of pleasing Allah hardens into custom and can turn harmful.

themes.label: Intention and sincerity (niyyah, ikhlas)
themes.note: Allah knows the heart, so doing deeds for Him rather than for one's group or for thanks is decisive.

themes.label: The purposes behind Allah's commands (maqasid)
themes.note: Means such as institutions and masjids must never become ends in themselves.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: Harshness over technical mistakes drives people away; build on what they already do.

themes.label: The Names and Attributes of Allah
themes.note: Tasbih as exaltation beyond praise, His kingship and power, and Al-Khaliq, Al-Bari and Al-Musawwir.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: Creation is purposeful and each person is designed for a purpose; those who know theirs live differently.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example
themes.note: The Prophet as a paradigm no one could explain away, to be emulated most where it is hardest.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: The Day of Taghabun reveals who was deceived and who deceived.

quran.point: People who follow their fathers even if the fathers understood nothing and had no guidance.
Al-Khaliq, Al-Bari, Al-Musawwir: the three names he explains to show creation is purposeful.

maxims: Once the means become the objective, you're corrupt
The masjid is not the goal; it is a means
Exalting is claiming no flaw I can point out
Al-Musawwir is the granter of purpose
Emulate him where it hurts
Could you do it and never be thanked?

stories.who: The engagement procession in the Middle East
stories.point: A custom meant to guarantee both families' accountability turned into showing off once its purpose was forgotten.

stories.who: A young man in Syria who prayed only Fajr
stories.point: Scolding drove him away while encouragement added a prayer; remember the purpose before the technicality.

stories.who: The Prophet as seen by his contemporaries
stories.point: His selflessness was so unexplainable that people either fled or bound themselves to him.

contemporary: Masjids and Islamic institutions that pursue expansion for its own sake
His Ramadan series on reduced concepts
Group, ethnic and national loyalties in community work
takeaways: Regularly ask why you do each religious practice and whether it is achieving its purpose
Treat institutions, including the masjid, as means and close or change them when they stop serving
Encourage people from where they are instead of scolding technical mistakes
Work out your purpose and emulate the Prophet especially in your hardest relationships and habits
Before claiming you did something for Allah, check whether you could bear never being thanked
